# Implementation Plan: Codex Raw-Autoconnect Phase 1 — Self-Onboard, Codex-Owned Daemon Lifecycle, Hard Diagnosed Errors
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"codex-autoconnect-self-contained-zero-friction"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-24. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <job_dir>/plan.md`.*

> **SCOPE: PHASE 1 ONLY (server-agnostic, codex-submodule-only).** Phase 2 (the embedded Rust
> transport-swap session server), Phase 3 (app/wire plain-WS adapter), and Phase 4 (cross-machine app
> discovery) are explicitly **out of scope** and deferred. This plan makes raw-codex `/remote on`
> self-onboarding + daemon-lifecycle-owning + honestly-diagnosed, independent of the eventual server
> language. Seeded from brainstorm
> `.ralph/brainstorms/codex-autoconnect-self-contained-zero-friction/rust-crate-brainstorm-synthesis.md`
> (operator decision 2026-06-23: Node-free is HARD-REQUIRED → Rust server committed for Phase 2, gated
> on a live BOOX transport spike). The committed `selected-direction.md` is from the **voided**
> bundled-Node-sidecar iteration; its **Phase 1 sub-scope is identical** to the rust-crate decomposition
> and is authoritative here, but its Phase 2 framing is superseded.

## Overview

Today, raw codex (the fork) ships a native Happy client (`codex-rs-overlay/codex-happy/`) that can mirror
a codex session to the Happy mobile app E2EE over the per-machine session plane (`127.0.0.1:<tunnelPort>`
from `~/.happy/machine.json`). But the **zero-friction first run is incomplete**: codex only attaches
when `~/.happy` credentials AND `machine.json` already exist — both of which are produced today only by
the **Node happy-cli daemon** (`happy daemon start`). If they're absent, `/remote on` either prints a
static "run `happy` once" hint (creds-absent) or the attach **silently falls back to vanilla codex**
(daemon/listener unreachable). The GitHub device-flow onboarding code that would mint codex's own creds
already exists in `onboard.rs` but is **built and unwired**.

Phase 1 closes the local zero-friction gap with three changes, all server-agnostic and codex-only:

1. **Self-onboard** — wire `onboard.rs`'s device flow into `/remote on` when `credentials_ready()` is
   false, so codex mints its own `~/.happy` creds with no happy-cli. (+ the M1 `access.key` `0o600` fix.)
2. **Codex-owned daemon lifecycle** — a server-agnostic supervisor seam so codex starts / health-probes
   / restarts / stops the per-machine daemon itself (driving the existing Node `happy daemon start` now;
   the Phase 2 Rust server slots in behind the same trait with no caller changes).
3. **Hard diagnosed errors** — replace the silent fallback-to-vanilla on a `/remote on` *intent* with a
   clear, categorized `/remote` error (no-creds vs no-daemon vs session/connect failure) that tells the
   user *why*.

### Codebase Context
*(Seeded from brainstorm `selected-direction.md` + `rust-crate-brainstorm-synthesis.md`; grounded by
first-hand source reads and the parallel `researcher`/`architect`/codex/copilot research briefs.)*

  module doc (onboard.rs:20-22) explicitly states "the interactive surfacing of the device code
  (display + browser open) and the decision of *when* to onboard are owned by the attach layer (US-006);
  this module provides the mechanism." Device-code display helper: `DeviceCode::display_uri` (:70).
  `OnboardError` enum (:100) already categorizes Transport/DeviceFlow/Decode/Io. Tests at
  `onboard_tests.rs` (parameterized `github_base_url` for hermetic coverage; SANDBOX-PATCH'd egress).
- **`codex/codex-rs-overlay/codex-happy/src/attach.rs`** — `maybe_attach` (:118) returns the tap sender

  `HAPPY_CURRENT_SESSION_ID` env (happy-cli already owns the session). `credentials_ready()` (:140)
  mirrors the establish gate (`read_credentials` + `read_machine_state` both present). `run_attach` (:147)
  drains events while `establish` (:343) runs under an 8s `CONNECT_BUDGET` (:74); on
  `Ok(None) | Err(_)` (:167-169) it **silently returns** (fallback to vanilla). `establish` returns
  `Option` and collapses every failure (no creds :347, no machine :348, session-create :357-359,
  connect :376) into `None` — **the lost diagnostic signal**.
- **`codex/codex-rs-overlay/codex-happy/src/auth.rs`** — `happy_home_dir` (:25, `$HAPPY_HOME_DIR` or

  tunnel_port, loopback_port, tunnel_id, last_tunnel_url }`), `MachineState::tunnel_local_base_url`
  (:84). These define what the lifecycle supervisor must produce/await.
- **`/remote on` command seam (upstream-canonical TUI, SANDBOX-PATCH'd):**
  - `tui/src/chatwidget/slash_dispatch.rs` — `SlashCommand::Remote` "on"/"off" arms (~:720-753): "on"
    calls `set_feature_enabled(Feature::RemoteSession, true)`, then **if `credentials_ready()`** sends

    Bare `/remote` reports state (~:382-392).
  - `tui/src/app/event_dispatch.rs` — `apply_remote_session_toggle` (:27-45): on enable, if

  - `tui/src/app_event.rs` — `AppEvent::SetRemoteSession{enabled}` (:200-207).
  - `tui/src/chatwidget/settings.rs` — `set_feature_enabled` (:69).
- **TUI surfacing primitives (confirmed by researcher):** `add_info_message(...)` is the user-facing
  info/progress primitive (chatwidget.rs). **A browser-open helper already exists** —
  `webbrowser::open(...)` is used in `tui/src/onboarding/auth.rs:1-75` and `tui/src/app/history_ui.rs`,
  so onboarding can open the verification URL with NO new dependency. The clean precedent for a
  background-task → TUI surfacing round-trip is `SlashCommand::Diff` (slash_dispatch.rs:393-417): it

  (spawn the device-flow poll, send an `AppEvent` carrying the user-code/URL and the final

- **Unix-perms precedent (for the M1 0o600 fix):** `codex/codex-rs-overlay/codex-copilot/src/auth.rs:263-266`

- **Daemon-lifecycle reference (server-agnostic; happy-cli, REFERENCE ONLY — not edited):** the concrete

### Technical Constraints
- **codex/CLAUDE.md tenet 1 (minimize upstream-canonical conflict surface):** prefer new overlay files
  in `codex-rs-overlay/codex-happy/`; any edit to `external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/` needs a
  `// SANDBOX PATCH:` marker + a row in the codex **wrapper** patch-surface doc + a rebase-replant note.
  That doc is `docs/implementation/patch-surface.md` **relative to the codex submodule root** (=
  `codex/docs/implementation/patch-surface.md` from the codexu repo root — the file with the 24
  remote_session references), **NOT** the nested `external/repos/codex-patched/docs/implementation/
  patch-surface.md` (which has none). The existing remote_session seams are registered there at
  `patch-surface.md:979-1040` (the "Happy native remote-session overlay egress — US-008" block,
  invariants 54-59; invariant 59 is the `/remote on|off` command seam). The new onboard/lifecycle/
  diagnosed-error seams extend that block (US-009 absorbed).
- **8s `CONNECT_BUDGET`** in attach.rs bounds the steady-state attach; the device-flow poll (up to
  `expires_in`, typically ~15 min) and daemon-start latency must NOT run inside that budget — onboarding
  + daemon-start are a `/remote on`-driven *pre-step*, separate from the per-attach connect timeout.
- **Unix-only `0o600` — secure CREATION, not just chmod-after-write (F-007):** the chmod must be
  `cfg(unix)`-gated (Windows no-op), AND the secret must never transit a world-readable file. The atomic
  write in `onboard.rs::write_json_atomically` writes a `*.tmp` then renames; a plain `fs::write` creates
  the tmp with default umask perms, leaving a readable window before any post-rename chmod. The fix is to
  create the temp file itself at `0o600` (Unix) — e.g. `OpenOptions::new().write(true).create(true)
  .mode(0o600)` (the `codex-copilot/src/auth.rs:263-266` precedent) — so the secret is owner-only from
  first byte. Scope the secure-create to the `access.key` write (profile.json/settings.json are not
  secret).
- **`should_skip_attach`** (HAPPY_SESSION_ENV) must remain the idempotency guard — onboarding/lifecycle
  only runs when codex owns the session, never when happy-cli already does.
- **Server-agnostic boundary:** Phase 1 drives the **Node** `happy daemon start`. On a machine with no
  happy-cli, there is no Phase-1 daemon to start (the Node-free Rust daemon is Phase 2) — so the
  lifecycle seam must hard-diagnose "no daemon available" rather than hang or silently fall back. (See
  Open Questions.)

## Approach

### Architecture

Three concerns, layered so Phase 2 (Rust server) drops in with no caller changes:

1. **Onboarding driver (new overlay module, `codex-happy/src/remote_on.rs`).** A small async orchestrator
   the `/remote on` seam calls when `credentials_ready()` is false. It runs `request_device_code` →
   surfaces `user_code` + `display_uri()` to the user (via `add_info_message` from the arm) and
   best-effort `webbrowser::open(...)` → `poll_for_token` → `complete_onboard_with_token`. Surfacing is
   done through an injected callback/trait so the module stays decoupled from codex-core's TUI types and
   is unit-testable (mirrors how `attach.rs` defines a local `AppServerHandle` trait for test fakes).
   **DECIDED control flow (resolves Q2 — F-002/F-004/F-009):** the `/remote on` "on" arm drives this
   **inline + on a background task** (the `SlashCommand::Diff` → `tokio::spawn` precedent) and, on
   onboard success, sends the **existing** `AppEvent::SetRemoteSession{enabled:true}` to attach via
   `apply_remote_session_toggle`/`maybe_attach`. A NEW result-bearing `AppEvent` variant is added ONLY
   if the diagnosed error / device-code surfacing cannot be done from the arm via `add_info_message`
   (last resort — minimize upstream-canonical surface). There must be exactly ONE attach path; do not
   create a duplicate.

2. **Daemon supervisor (new overlay module, `codex-happy/src/daemon_supervisor.rs`).** A server-agnostic
   trait, e.g.:
   ```rust
   pub trait SessionPlaneSupervisor {
       fn ensure_running(&self) -> impl Future<Output = Result<MachineState, SupervisorError>> + Send;
       fn health(&self) -> impl Future<Output = SupervisorHealth> + Send;
       fn stop(&self) -> impl Future<Output = ()> + Send;
   }
   ```
   The Phase-1 impl `NodeDaemonSupervisor` shells out to the existing **`happy daemon start-sync`**
   (detached) path — when `happy` is on PATH — and probes readiness (below). Phase 2's
   `EmbeddedRustSupervisor` will implement the same trait — callers (`establish` / `/remote on`) bind to
   the trait, not the Node impl.
   - **OWNERSHIP RULE (F-005, critical):** codex must NOT stop or restart a per-machine daemon it did
     NOT start. The Node daemon is a SHARED singleton (one per machine, serving any happy-cli/mobile
     sessions). `ensure_running()` must be **start-if-absent + health-probe only** — if a daemon is
     ALREADY running (state file present, ports bound), codex attaches to it and never touches its
     lifecycle. `stop()`/restart apply ONLY to a daemon THIS codex process started (track ownership,
     e.g. via whether codex spawned it / `daemon.state.json` identity), or are **deferred to Phase 2**
     (the embedded Rust server codex exclusively owns). Stopping a foreign daemon would disrupt existing
     Happy sessions — explicitly forbidden in Phase 1.
   - **Readiness contract (F-008, accurate to codex's needs):** codex's session attach uses the **tunnel
     listener** (`127.0.0.1:<tunnelPort>`, NO auth header — auth.rs:84-86 + the US-001 live de-risk
     note); the loopback listener + `X-Loopback-Capability` is happy-cli-internal and NOT used by codex's
     autoconnect. So readiness = `machine.json` present with a valid `tunnelPort` AND a TCP probe of
     `tunnelPort` succeeds (optionally also probe `loopbackPort` as a "fully bound" signal). Do not gate
     codex readiness on the loopback capability. The supervisor must distinguish **"starting"**
     (retry/wait with a bounded budget, NOT the 8s `CONNECT_BUDGET`) from **"dead/absent"** (→
     `SupervisorError`/`NoDaemon`).

3. **Typed diagnosed error.** Replace `establish()`'s `Option` return with `Result<(SessionClient,
   InboundReceiver), AttachError>` where `AttachError` distinguishes `NoCredentials`, `NoDaemon`/
   `ListenerUnreachable`, `SessionCreateFailed`, `ConnectFailed`. `maybe_attach`'s **constructor-time**
   call keeps treating any error as a silent vanilla fallback (don't break non-remote-on startup), but
   the **`/remote on` intent** path surfaces the diagnosed error to the user. This is the key behavioral
   split: *intent → loud; passive startup → quiet*.

### Implementation Strategy

**Prerequisites (impl-time, F-003):** the codex changes land in the `codex/` submodule. Before
implementation, init submodules (`git submodule update --init --recursive`) and create a codex submodule
worktree (`.ralph/jobs/<job>/codex-worktree/` or `codex/.worktrees/<task>`) per
`packages/happy-cli/AGENTS.md` "Codex Submodule Edits" — do NOT edit the codex submodule inside the
plan worktree (its submodule is uninitialized).

**Ship mechanics (F-006, repo workflow requirement — not optional):** codex submodule changes use the
**two-commit + pointer-bump** discipline: (1) commit the codex-side changes in the codex submodule
worktree and push to the codex remote (`gim-home/codex`); (2) a SEPARATE codexu parent commit bumps the
`codex/` submodule gitlink. The parent commit can only record a SHA — never mix uncommitted submodule
edits into it. Every upstream-canonical edit carries a `// SANDBOX PATCH:` marker + a wrapper
patch-surface.md row + a rebase-replant note. (This is PLAN-ONLY; the impl member executes it.)

Ordered (see Story Decomposition + Suggested Decomposition):
1. **US-001** — M1 `0o600` perms fix (isolated, foundational, already has a test module).
2. **US-002** — typed `AttachError` + diagnosed `/remote on` error path (replaces silent fallback on
   intent). Establishes the error plumbing the onboard + lifecycle stories report through.
3. **US-003** — wire `onboard.rs` device flow into `/remote on` creds-absent case (new onboard driver
   module + TUI surfacing + browser open + poll).
4. **US-004** — codex-owned daemon lifecycle supervisor seam (server-agnostic), integrated so
   `/remote on` ensures the daemon is up (after onboard) before attaching, and reports `NoDaemon`
   through US-002's error path when it can't.

## Scope
### In Scope
- Wire `onboard.rs` device flow into `/remote on` (creds-absent), incl. interactive user-code/URL
  surfacing + browser open + token poll + `complete_onboard_with_token`. (Absorbs
  `codex-autoconnect-interactive-self-onboard-remote-on`.)
- M1: `~/.happy/access.key` `0o600` on Unix.
- Server-agnostic codex-owned daemon lifecycle seam (start-if-absent / health-probe; stop/restart only
  for a codex-owned child) driving the existing Node daemon; Rust server slots in at Phase 2.
- Hard diagnosed `/remote on` error (no-creds / no-daemon / session/connect failure); no silent vanilla
  fallback on a remote-on intent.
- Overlay-first edits + patch-surface registration for any upstream-canonical seam.

### Out of Scope
- Phase 2: embedded Rust session-server crate. Phase 3: app/wire plain-WS adapter. Phase 4: cross-machine
  app discovery.
- Any `packages/` (codexu) code edits (reading happy-cli daemon source for the seam contract is fine).
- The clean-machine *live* `/remote on` spike + release build/packaging (impl-time verification, not
  plan; and codex daemon-bringup on a Node-free machine is Phase 2).

## Risk Areas
- **Long-poll vs TUI responsiveness:** the device flow polls for minutes; must run as a background task
  surfacing progress, never blocking the prompt (reuse the attach background-task pattern).
- **Partial-state on failure:** onboard succeeds (creds written) but daemon-start fails → the diagnosed
  error must be actionable and not leave a half-attached session; idempotent re-run of `/remote on`.
- **Foreign-daemon disruption (F-005):** the Node daemon is a shared machine singleton; codex stopping/
  restarting a daemon it did not start would kill other happy-cli/mobile sessions. Phase-1 supervisor is
  start-if-absent + health only; stop/restart is codex-owned-child-only or deferred to Phase 2.
- **Shared hot files:** US-002/US-003/US-004 all touch `slash_dispatch.rs` + `attach.rs` → serialize.
- **Rebase fragility:** new upstream-canonical seams in `slash_dispatch.rs` add conflict surface; keep
  edits 1-3 lines calling into overlay code; register in the wrapper `patch-surface.md`.
- **Node-free Phase-1 gap:** without happy-cli there's no Phase-1 daemon (Rust is Phase 2) — the
  supervisor must hard-diagnose `NoDaemon`, not hang. (Open Question Q1.)

## Acceptance Criteria
- With creds absent (test uses a temp `HAPPY_HOME_DIR` fixture — NOT the developer's real `~/.happy`,
  F-011), `/remote on` runs the device flow, surfaces user-code + URL, opens the browser (best-effort
  with text-only fallback), and on completion writes `access.key` (secure-created at `0o600` on Unix —
  F-007) + `profile.json` + seeds `machineId` — verified by a unit/integration test using the
  parameterized `github_base_url` hermetic harness.
- `establish()` returns a typed `AttachError`; the `/remote on` intent path surfaces a categorized,
  actionable message (no-creds / no-daemon / connect-fail); the constructor-time attach path keeps the
  silent vanilla fallback (no regression to non-remote-on startup).
- A server-agnostic `SessionPlaneSupervisor` trait exists with a `NodeDaemonSupervisor` impl; `/remote on`
  calls `ensure_running()` after onboard and attaches only on a ready listener (`machine.json` +
  `tunnelPort` probe). The supervisor is **start-if-absent + health only** and never stops/restarts a
  daemon codex did not start (F-005).
- **`NoDaemon` is exercised by a test (F-010):** after a successful self-onboard, when no daemon binary
  is available (happy-cli not on PATH) and no daemon is running, `/remote on` reports a categorized
  `NoDaemon` error (no hang, no silent vanilla fallback) — verified with an injected spawner/PATH-probe
  fake.
- All codex edits are overlay-first; every upstream-canonical seam carries a `// SANDBOX PATCH:` marker
  + a wrapper `codex/docs/implementation/patch-surface.md` row + a rebase-replant note.
- `cargo check --workspace` (from `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs`) passes; `just test -p
  codex-happy` (+ `-p codex-tui` if the TUI seam changed) passes; `just fmt` clean.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition
- **US-001 — M1 `access.key` `0o600` (Unix).** `onboard.rs::write_credentials` creates the secret file
  (incl. its temp file) at `0o600` on Unix (secure-create, NOT chmod-after-write — F-007); extend
  `onboard_tests.rs` (temp `HAPPY_HOME_DIR` fixture). Small.
- **US-002 — Typed `AttachError` + diagnosed `/remote on` error.** `establish` → `Result`; intent path
  surfaces categorized error; constructor path stays silent. Touches `attach.rs` + `slash_dispatch.rs`
  (reuse existing `AppEvent`; new variant only if unavoidable). Medium.
- **US-003 — Self-onboard wiring.** New onboard-driver module (device-code surfacing + browser open +
  poll + complete), driven inline from the `/remote on` arm on a background task; on success sends the
  existing `AppEvent::SetRemoteSession` to attach. Touches new module + `slash_dispatch.rs` + `lib.rs`.
  Medium.
- **US-004 — Server-agnostic daemon lifecycle supervisor.** New `daemon_supervisor.rs` (trait +
  `NodeDaemonSupervisor` spawning `happy daemon start-sync` + readiness probe of `machine.json` +
  `tunnelPort`); **start-if-absent + health only; never stop/restart a daemon codex did not start**
  (F-005); integrate into the `/remote on` flow + `establish` so codex ensures a ready listener; report
  `NoDaemon` (incl. happy-cli-not-on-PATH) via US-002. Medium/large.

## Suggested Decomposition

### Cluster: codex-autoconnect-phase1-serial
- Stories: [US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004]
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`codex-rs-overlay/codex-happy/src/attach.rs`,
  `external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/slash_dispatch.rs`,
  `codex-rs-overlay/codex-happy/src/lib.rs`]; exclusive=[US-001 → `onboard.rs`/`onboard_tests.rs`;
  US-003 → `remote_on.rs`; US-004 → `daemon_supervisor.rs`]; risk=high (shared upstream-canonical hot

## Open Questions
- **Q1 (central, server-agnostic boundary):** In Phase 1 the only daemon to "own" is the **Node**
  `happy daemon start`, which requires happy-cli on PATH. On a truly Node-free machine (only codex
  installed), there is NO Phase-1 daemon — the Node-free Rust daemon is Phase 2. Confirm Phase 1's
  intended boundary: codex's supervisor drives the Node daemon *when happy-cli is present*, and otherwise
  emits the hard diagnosed `NoDaemon` error ("no per-machine session server available; install happy-cli
  or wait for the embedded server"). Self-onboard (creds) DOES work Node-free; only the daemon does not.
- **Q2 (DECIDED — F-002/F-004/F-009):** The `/remote on` control flow is settled: drive onboard + the
  diagnosed error **inline from the `/remote on` arm** on a background task, and on success send the
  EXISTING `AppEvent::SetRemoteSession{enabled:true}` to attach (reusing `apply_remote_session_toggle` →
  `maybe_attach`). A new result-bearing `AppEvent` variant is added ONLY if the device-code/diagnosed
  error genuinely cannot be surfaced via `add_info_message` from the arm — last resort, to minimize
  upstream-canonical surface. There must be exactly one attach path. (Captured in Approach > Architecture.)
- **Q3 (RESOLVED by research):** ~~Browser-open dependency~~ — the codex-rs TUI already vends
  `webbrowser::open(...)` (`tui/src/onboarding/auth.rs`, `tui/src/app/history_ui.rs`), so onboarding
  surfaces the verification URL + user code AND auto-opens the browser with NO new dependency. Keep a
  text-only fallback when `webbrowser::open` errors (headless/SSH).
- **Q4:** Dev Tunnel bring-up — the brainstorm lists "bring up the Dev Tunnel" under Phase 1 lifecycle.
  The Node daemon already owns tunnel startup as part of `happy daemon start`. Confirm codex's supervisor
  only *triggers + awaits* the Node daemon's tunnel (not a separate codex-owned `devtunnel host`).
